title: Time-budget experiment
question: On a free-tier server (512 MB, no swap, 0.1 CPU), how close does the optimizer get to the best known plan, and how fast?
design: Each contractor solved at 10, 60, 300 and 600 s, 3 repeats, limited and unlimited, plus one 30-minute unlimited reference. 50 runs, about 4.5 hours. Limits applied with systemd cgroups in WSL.

title: Query-budget experiment
question: How few real travel-time queries (each stop's K nearest stops plus its leg to campus, the rest estimated) still give routes within 3% of the full matrix?
design: K = 0, 3, 5, 10, 20, 40 with two estimators (straight-line fit, shortest path through queried legs) plus the full matrix as control; 2 contractors, 3 repeats, 60 s unlimited search. Plans are scored on real OSRM times. 72 runs, about 40 minutes on 2 cores.

title: Pipeline test
question: Does the whole experiment pipeline work? 5 s runs, about 1 minute. Not a reported result.
design: One 5 s run per contractor and setup, plus a 10 s reference.

title: Query-budget pipeline test
question: Does the query-budget pipeline work? 5 s runs, about 20 seconds. Not a reported result.
design: K = 10 with both estimators plus the full matrix, 1 repeat.

title: Traffic check
question: If every travel time is 1.3 or 1.5 times longer (morning traffic), can the optimizer still keep every student under 90 minutes, and does it still beat the current routes?
design: Travel times x1.0 (control), x1.3 and x1.5, stop times unchanged. Each contractor planned and scored on the scaled times, 3 repeats, 60 s unlimited. 18 runs, about 10 minutes. Judged at x1.5 on the worst run.

title: Seed check
question: With the synthetic students redrawn from other seeds, is the improvement over the current routes still there?
design: Seed 2026 (the frozen dataset, control) plus students redrawn with seeds 2027, 2028 and 2029; same stops, routes, buses and travel times. One 60 s unlimited run per contractor and seed. 8 runs, about 5 minutes. Judged on the new seeds, worst run.

title: Traffic check pipeline test
question: Does the traffic-check pipeline work? 5 s runs, about 15 seconds. Not a reported result.

title: Seed check pipeline test
question: Does the seed-check pipeline work? 5 s runs, about 15 seconds. Not a reported result.

title: Optimizer scaling
question: How do the optimizer's build time, memory and plan quality grow as stops and buses grow, and does handing OR-Tools the travel times as a matrix instead of a Python callback change that?
design: Instances Jadoon (171 stops), Nadeem (143), All (311, both fleets), All-doubled (622), and Jadoon-doubled (342) and Nadeem-doubled (286); a doubled instance copies every stop 30 s from its original and every bus, so it tests model size, not geography. Lookups callback and matrix; 300 s each, no limits, each run a fresh process: 12 runs, about an hour. No pass/fail threshold: it reports curves. All and All-doubled need the combined matrix (OSRM) and are recorded as skipped without it; the doubled contractor instances stand in for size until then. Peak memory is the OS's figure for the machine that ran it (Linux ru_maxrss, Windows peak working set).

title: Rerouting quality pass
question: When a road on a bus's route is closed, how much does letting students walk to another stop gain over the patched published route, beyond what skipping a stop saves on a normal day, and is the fast greedy method close to the exact one?
design: Every frozen scenario (about 210: two 200 m full-block closures per route, two bus positions each, plus the historical Shahrah-e-Faisal block and University Road ponding, reported apart) x walking limits 0, 400 and 800 m x R0 (patched route), R2 (greedy, then improvement rounds) and R3 (exact) on true OSRM times with no time limit. At 400 m two more arms: the no-closure control (same solve on unblocked times) and must-serve (25% of stops, fixed draw). Judged on synthetic scenarios with at least 2 remaining stops where R0 loses at least 60 s: median closure-specific gain at least 60 s; R2 within 60 s of R3 in 90% of scenarios and on every route's median; no failed run. runs_total is set by the script from the scenario file (5 rows per scenario).

title: Rerouting limits pass
question: On a free-tier server (512 MB, no swap, 0.1 CPU), with the road graph already loaded, how fast does the rerouter have a valid plan, and how close to the oracle is it at 30 s?
design: Every scenario at 400 m. One worker process per route, arm and repeat loads the graph once and solves that route's scenarios in turn. Arms: plan on the road graph under the limits with a 30 s cap (3 repeats, judged); plan on the graph with no limits (graph error alone); plan on true times under the limits (time limit alone). Every plan is scored on true times against the oracle (R3 on true times, no limit). Judged on the worst repeat: a valid plan within 5 s in 95% of judged scenarios; within 60 s of the oracle at 30 s in 90%; peak memory under 400 MB including the graph. Limits applied with systemd cgroups in WSL; runs_total is set by the script (7 rows per scenario).

title: Rerouting scaling
question: How do decision time and memory grow with stops on one bus, with the size of the road graph searched, and with the number of buses one closure hits at once, and what does solving in slices cost?
design: Stops: synthetic problems with 4 to 20 remaining stops and 1, 2 or 4 extra boarding points per stop, 3 seeds, limited and unlimited (R3 not run above 16 stops; a lower bound instead). Graph: 10, 30 and 60 points on the longest route's corridor and on the whole city, limited and unlimited. Buses: the Shahrah-e-Faisal closure hitting 1, 5, 10 and 20 buses in one limited process sharing the row cache. Slices: the three largest judged scenarios solved 256 masks at a time, with plan quality and saved-state size after each slice. Each measurement runs in a fresh process. No pass/fail threshold: it reports curves.

title: Rerouting quality pipeline test
question: Does the rerouting quality pipeline work? Three hand-checkable toy scenarios, a few seconds. Not a reported result.
design: data/scenarios_toy.json (written by 'run_reroute.py make-toy'): the plan's toy, the same with no walking pair, and one with a stop inside the closure. 15 rows.

title: Rerouting limits pipeline test
question: Does the rerouting limits pipeline work? Toy scenarios, plans on true times only (the toy file has no road graph), a few seconds. Not a reported result.
design: The truth_limited arm on the three toy scenarios, one repeat, inside the systemd limits (needs WSL with systemd; on another machine run it by hand with --no-limits).

title: Optimizer scaling pipeline test
question: Does the optimizer scaling pipeline work? Nadeem only, 10 s, both lookups. Not a reported result.
design: Nadeem x callback and matrix, 10 s each, about half a minute.

title: Rerouting scaling pipeline test
question: Does the rerouting scaling pipeline work? A few seconds. Not a reported result.
design: Stops at 4 and 8 on synthetic problems without limits, and solving in slices on the two judged toy scenarios.

title: Rerouting scaling, first run (greedy-only R2)
question: Evidence kept from the first RS1 'stops' run, before R2 gained its improvement rounds (logbook, 17 November). Superseded by Rerouting scaling.
design: Synthetic problems, 4 to 20 stops, 1, 2 or 4 candidates per stop, 3 seeds, unlimited, on code 7299036. Do not rerun: the current code gives the rerun's results.
